_what: Rate card for the models the benchmark legs actually use. Read off the LiteLLM admin UI's per-model detail pages on 2026-09-17. Consumed by reference/gen-cost-analysis.py; no generator may hardcode a price.
_amended: 2026-09-29: the four models above had all been WITHDRAWN from the gateway's catalogue -- `GET /v1/models` no longer lists any of them -- so they price past runs only and nothing new can be measured with them. The four `_added_2026_09_29` rows below replace them role for role and were read from the gateway's own unauthenticated `GET /public/litellm_model_cost_map`, not from the admin UI. Same basis either way: both report the upstream list rate (gpt-5-mini reads 0.25/2.00 in both), so rows from the two sources are comparable. A run priced with the new rows is NOT comparable with the v1.28 matrix -- every model differs.
_keys: Keyed by the EXACT `model` string in report.ndjson, which carries litellm's `openai/` routing prefix. That prefix is not part of the model's name -- the gateway strips it before resolving the alias in `public_name`.
_caveats: Input and output only. The UI's model pages expose no cached-input tier, so a cache-read discount -- if the gateway applies one -- is not modelled and every figure computed from this file is an upper bound on input cost.
Reasoning tokens are billed as output. gpt-5-mini is a reasoning model, and our llm_output_tokens already includes its exposed reasoning tokens, so no separate term is needed.
These are the gateway operator's posted rates, not an invoice. They are what a run WOULD cost at list price.

openai/Azure/gpt-4.1._also: The IBAC judge model (rossoctl-platform-config ibac.judgeModel). Its calls are NOT in report.ndjson -- see gen-cost-analysis.py's judge section.

openai/aws/claude-sonnet-5._role_2026_09_30: The tau2 role on BOTH profiles, and also registry.py's own model_override for tau2, so the *_LLM_MODEL_TAU2 values restate what the pod resolves anyway (set explicitly regardless: that variable is the only lever that displaces model_override without an image rebuild). CORRECTION to the 2026-09-29/30 notes: this model was believed WITHDRAWN from the vpc (internet) gateway and vpc-int-only, which made tau2 look un-matchable across platforms and moved legs #9/#10 onto aws/claude-sonnet-4-6 at twice the price. Both beliefs were wrong. `GET /v1/models` returns only what the calling KEY'S TEAM is granted, not the gateway catalogue -- the admin UI shows vpc serving aws/claude-sonnet-5 (bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5) at exactly this row, 1.52/7.60 -- and the run history said the same: the 29 ykt3-to-ykt2 tau2 runs through 2026-09-15 all ran sonnet-5 against that same vpc gateway. So tau2 tokens AND dollars compare across platforms again. Never conclude 'not served' from /v1/models; it can only tell you 'not granted to this key'.

openai/gemini-2.5-pro._assumed: Priced from the rate card's `gcp/gemini-2.5-pro` entry (vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-pro, $1.25/$10.00). Our legs send the BARE alias `gemini-2.5-pro`, which is a separate registration on the gateway and the only Gemini 2.5 Pro our key can see; `/model/info` is admin-only (403), so its backend was not read directly. If the bare alias is ever repointed, this row is the one that goes stale.

openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._added_2026_09_29: Replaces Azure/gpt-5-mini as the INSTANCE DEFAULT, so it prices gsm8k legs #1-#3 and #5-#8. Cheaper than the model it replaces on both directions (0.25/2.00), so a gsm8k leg's cost is not directly comparable with the v1.28 figure even at identical token counts.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._also: Also the IBAC judge model from 2026-09-29 (rossoctl-platform-config ibac.judgeModel), taking over from Azure/gpt-4.1. Judge calls are NOT in report.ndjson -- see gen-cost-analysis.py's judge section. The judge is now an order of magnitude cheaper per call than it was, which moves the plugin-overhead cost figures on its own, independently of any change in call COUNT.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._backend_not_read: `/model/info` is admin-only (403) for an ['llm_api_routes'] key, so which Azure deployment sits behind this alias was not read. `litellm_model` is therefore omitted rather than guessed.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-luna._role_2026_09_30: Not used for tau2: registry.py records that tau2 needs a Sonnet-class model (the old default gpt-5-mini scored ~0.1 on the same 10 tasks; the slower reasoning model gpt-5 gave 6/10 'timed out'), and aws/claude-sonnet-5 carries that role on both profiles. NOTE this is registry.py's recorded measurement, not something re-measured on 2026-09-30 -- luna's two tau2 runs that day hit the cache-hit bug in the top-level _tau2_task0_2026_09_30 note, which is model-independent, so they say nothing either way about luna's tau2 capability.

openai/azure/gpt-5.6-terra._added_2026_09_29: Replaces Azure/gpt-4.1 in the gsm8k model-swap leg (#4). Input matches what it replaces exactly (2.00); output is 12.00 against 8.00. Against the new default it is 10x input and 10x output, so it still plays the 'dearer rung' role the leg exists to measure -- but the RATIO changed (gpt-4.1 was 8x/4x over gpt-5-mini), which is the figure to re-derive rather than carry over.
openai/azure/gpt-5.6-terra._role_2026_09_30: Also the INTRANET (vpc-int) appworld role, because vpc-int serves no gemini. Priced identically to gcp/gemini-3.1-pro-preview (2.00/12.00), so appworld COST comparisons across platforms still hold even though the token counts belong to different models. Note this model now plays two roles on the intranet profile -- the gsm8k swap leg #4 and appworld #11/#12.

openai/aws/claude-sonnet-4-6._added_2026_09_29: Was briefly the tau2 model for legs #9/#10, on the belief that aws/claude-sonnet-5 had been withdrawn from the vpc catalogue and this was the only Sonnet left. WITHDRAWN AS A CHOICE 2026-09-30: that belief came from `GET /v1/models`, which lists only what the key's team is granted -- sonnet-5 is served, so tau2 went back to it. This row costs 2x sonnet-5 (3.00/15.00 vs 1.52/7.60), so the switch was paying double for nothing. Kept in the card because the 2026-09-30 tau2 runs were priced on it.
openai/aws/claude-sonnet-4-6._tau2_task0: See the top-level _tau2_task0_2026_09_30 note: those errors are a cache-hit bug, not a property of this model.

openai/gcp/gemini-3.1-pro-preview._added_2026_09_29: Replaces gemini-2.5-pro on the appworld legs (#11, #12); same family, two minor versions on. Unlike the row it replaces this is the gateway's PREFIXED registration, not a bare alias, so it is the name the cost map actually carries and needs no assumed-pricing note. A `-preview` alias is repointed by its vendor without warning -- re-read this row before pricing a new appworld run.

_tau2_task0_2026_09_30: TAU2 ERRORS FROM A BROKEN CACHE HIT, NOT FROM ANY MODEL -- root-caused 2026-09-30, so do not read it as a property of whichever model row it was measured on. The MCP pod re-enables a LiteLLM disk cache for the user simulator (tau2_shim.py, configure_litellm(cache_only=True)), shared across every session for the pod's life. In litellm 1.103.1 any cache HIT raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'soundfile' -- caching_handler._sync_get_cache calls _should_defer_streaming_cache_hit_callbacks, which imports the anthropic pass-through response_cache chain down to `import soundfile`, absent from the tau2 venv. Verified in the pod: that function raises for ANY argument. tau2 aborts ~70 ms in; the MCP action executor never learns and sits out a 600 s cap, so the task surfaces as 'Failed to execute action: timed out' with llm_count 1, llm_input_tokens 5054, tool_total_s 600.1 -- THAT triple is the fingerprint. WHICH TASKS: `exgentic mcp` opens a dummy session on task_ids[0] at startup to enumerate action types and that session drives a real simulator completion, so task 0 is primed on every fresh pod; on a RE-USED pod every task a previous run completed is primed too (measured 4-task leg: 0 and 1 errored, 2 and 3 normal). Not the model (failed on azure/gpt-5.6-luna x2, aws/claude-sonnet-4-6 x2, aws/claude-sonnet-5 x1), not the gateway or architecture (ykt5/amd64/vpc and KinD/arm64/vpc-int alike), not our timeouts (we send action_timeout=1000, task timeout was 1200), and NOT a moved image -- exgentic-mcp-tau2:latest was BUILT 2026-07-22, two months before v1.28, and the tau2 pin re-read in the pod is still v0.1.3 / 5ba9e3e5. What changed is the venv, which `exgentic mcp` resolves from PyPI at POD START rather than baking into the image, so a July image picked up litellm 1.103.1. FIXED IN THIS REPO: registry.py's tau2 tool_env now pins EXGENTIC_LITELLM_CACHING=false, which makes the guard unreachable -- needs a Service image rebuild to take effect. PRICING: until a rebuilt Service runs, use a (total - 1) denominator for tau2 on a FRESH deploy, never re-use a tau2 pod across runs, and count each errored task's ~5.1k input tokens as spend that bought no verdict.
